The gold mine is `tests/patterns/<lang>/`:\n  **paired files** `name.<ext>` (target code, with `# ruleid:`-style annotations) + `name.sgrep`\n  (the pattern) — e.g. `tests/patterns/python/ac_matching_dots.py` + `.sgrep`. Also\n  `tests/parsing/`, `tests/autofix/`, `tests/rules/`, `tests/taint_maturity/`.\n- (j) **Ellipsis (`...`) and deep-matching operators** that abstract over irrelevant code, typed\n  metavariables, and constant propagation during matching (\"semantic equivalences\").\n\n## Comby\n\n- (a) Structural search-and-replace for \"~every language\", written in OCaml. Repo:\n  <https://github.com/comby-tools/comby> (2.6k stars; site <https://comby.dev>).\n- (b) No real tree: parses **balanced-delimiter structure + string/comment syntax** per language\n  family, not a grammar — matching is over the raw text.\n- (c) Trivially lossless (it never leaves the original text; replacements are spliced spans).\n- (d) Template syntax with holes: `:[hole]`, `:[[word]]`, `:[hole\\n]`, etc., plus a small `where`\n  rule language (equality, regex match, nested match) — <https://comby.dev/docs/syntax-reference>.\n- (e) Yes — that's its entire purpose: `comby 'match template' 'rewrite template'`; supports in-place\n  rewrites, JSON match output, custom metasyntax.\n- (f) Dozens of language definitions (comment/string/delimiter conventions); `.generic` matcher for\n  anything else.\n- (g) Custom matchers/metasyntax definable; OCaml library `comby-kernel`.\n- (h) Apache-2.0.\n- (i) Tests: `test/common/` — alcotest/OCaml files per language and feature\n  (`test_c.ml`, `test_go.ml`, `test_generic.ml`, `test_nested_matches.ml`, `test_match_offsets.ml`,\n  `test_custom_metasyntax.ml`, …) with inline source/template/expected strings; plus\n  `test/test_special_matcher_cases.ml`.\n- (j) **Grammar-less structural matching** (balanced-parens model) that works on languages you have\n  no parser for — a useful fallback layer meta-language could add below tree-sitter.\n\n## GritQL (grit)\n\n- (a) Query language + engine for searching and modifying code, Rust, tree-sitter based. Repo:\n  <https://github.com/getgrit/gritql> (4.5k stars; docs <https://docs.grit.io/language/overview>).\n- (b) Read-only trees with rewrite effects collected and applied to text (the engine tracks\n  \"effects\" rather than mutating the CST).\n- (c) Tree-sitter-grade source fidelity; rewrites preserve surrounding bytes and auto-fix\n  indentation.\n- (d) **GritQL**: declarative datalog-ish/logic-flavored language where *source snippets in\n  backticks are first-class patterns* (`` `console.log($msg)` ``), with metavariables, `where`\n  clauses, pattern composition (`and`/`or`/`not`/`contains`/`within`/`after`), named pattern\n  definitions, list/regex predicates, and built-in functions.\n- (e) Yes: `=>` rewrite operator inside patterns; `grit apply`; migration \"workflows\" (multi-step,\n  JS-scriptable — partly in the `js`/`python` dirs).\n- (f) ~20 target languages via tree-sitter (JS/TS, Python, Java, Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, CSS, JSON,\n  YAML, HCL, Solidity, SQL, …) listed in `crates/language`.\n- (g) Shareable pattern libraries (`.grit/patterns`); the standard library lives at\n  <https://github.com/getgrit/stdlib> (`.grit/patterns/<lang>/*.md`); custom language support\n  requires engine work.\n- (h) MIT (engine). stdlib has no SPDX-detected license (custom/none reported by GitHub API —\n  **unverified** what applies).\n- (i) Tests: `crates/core/src/test.rs` + `crates/core/src/snapshots/` (insta snapshots),\n  `crates/cli_bin/tests` + `crates/cli_bin/fixtures`. Repo: <https://github.com/srcML/srcML> (155 stars; site <https://www.srcml.org>).\n- (b) The XML document is freely mutable with any XML tooling; srcML converts both directions.\n- (c) **Fully lossless by design**: all text, whitespace, and comments are preserved inside the XML;\n  `srcml file.xml` regenerates the original source byte-for-byte.\n- (d) **XPath** (plus XSLT/XQuery) over the srcML namespace — reuses the entire XML ecosystem.\n- (e) Transformations via XSLT or DOM manipulation, then unparse back to source.\n- (f) C, C++, C#, Java officially; the develop-branch test suite shows Python and Objective-C\n  support in progress (`*_py.py.xml`, `*_m.m.xml` files).\n- (g) New languages require new parsers in the C++ codebase; output schema is a documented XML\n  vocabulary.\n- (h) GPL-3.0.\n- (i) Tests: `test/parser/testsuite/` — **thousands of single-construct `.xml` files** named\n  `construct_lang.ext.xml` (e.g. `assert_java.java.xml`, `atomic_c.c.xml`, `block_lambda.cpp.xml`),\n  each containing the source fragment and its expected markup; plus `test/client/` and\n  `test/libsrcml/`.\n- (j) Round-trip **source⇆document model with off-the-shelf query languages** (XPath/XSLT); the\n  per-construct round-trip testsuite layout is directly portable to meta-language's\n  `LANGUAGE_FIXTURES`.\n\n## difftastic\n\n- (a) Structural (syntax-aware) diff tool, Rust, built on tree-sitter. per-language `*-test` modules use\n  `RewriteTest`'s `rewriteRun(java(\"before\",\"after\"))` inline before/after style.\n- (j) **Type attribution inside a lossless tree** and the **TCK pattern**: a parser-independent\n  conformance suite — exactly the artifact meta-language should imitate (and can port from).\n\n## Spoon\n\n- (a) Java metaprogramming library (INRIA): analyze + transform Java source via a well-designed AST\n  (\"CtModel\"). Repo: <https://github.com/INRIA/spoon> (1.9k stars).\n- (b) **Mutable** AST with setters/factories; processors visit and mutate.\n- (c) Default pretty-printer reformats; the **`SniperJavaPrettyPrinter`**\n  (`src/main/java/spoon/support/sniper/SniperJavaPrettyPrinter.java`, verified) preserves original\n  formatting of unmodified elements — \"sniper mode\" prints only what changed.\n- (d) Typed queries: `model.getElements(new TypeFilter<>(CtMethod.class))`, composable `Filter`s and\n  `CtQuery` chains; also `spoon-smpl` (SmPL/Coccinelle-style semantic patches for Java).\n- (e) Processors, templates (`CtTemplate`), pattern matching/generation (`spoon.pattern`) with\n  parameterized snippets.\n- (f) Java only (+ Javadoc module, control/dataflow companions).\n- (g) Processor plugin model; Maven plugin.\n- (h) Dual CeCILL-C / MIT (verified: `LICENSE-CECILL-C.txt`, `LICENSE-MIT.txt`).\n- (i) Tests: `src/test/java/spoon/test/<feature>/` (hundreds of feature packages) with inputs under\n  `src/test/resources/`; sniper-printer round-trip tests are the interesting port target\n  (`src/test/java/spoon/test/prettyprinter/`).\n- (j) **Pattern objects built from compilable template code** (type-checked templates) and sniper\n  printing as a pluggable printer strategy.\n\n## JavaParser\n\n- (a) Java 1–25 parser + AST with symbol resolution (JavaSymbolSolver). Repo:\n  <https://github.com/javaparser/javaparser> (6.1k stars).\n- (b) Mutable AST (observable nodes).\n- (c) Optional **`LexicalPreservingPrinter`**\n  (`javaparser-core/src/main/java/com/github/javaparser/printer/lexicalpreservation/`, verified):\n  tracks tokens/whitespace and computes diffs (`Difference.java`, `DifferenceElementCalculator.java`)\n  so unmodified code keeps formatting; default printer reformats.\n- (d) Visitors + `Node.findAll(Class)`; no pattern language.\n- (e) Direct AST mutation; no rule/codemod framework.\n- (f) Java only.\n- (g) Library-level; symbol solver pluggable type solvers.\n- (h) Triple-licensed Apache-2.0 / LGPL / GPL (verified: `LICENSE.APACHE`, `LICENSE.LGPL`,\n  `LICENSE.GPL`).\n- (i) Tests: `javaparser-core-testing/src/test/java/com/github/javaparser/` — note\n  `LexicalPreservingPrinterTest` area, `TokenRangeTest.java`, `PositionMappingTest.java`,\n  `ParseErrorRecoveryTest.java`, plus issue-numbered regression tests (`Issue1017Test.java`, …) and\n  `ast/` construct tests; BDD suite in `javaparser-core-testing-bdd`.\n- (j) **Lexical preservation as a retrofit**: a token-diff algorithm bolted onto a non-lossless AST —\n  meta-language avoids this by being lossless-first, but its `Difference*` test cases are great\n  adversarial inputs.\n\n## Rascal MPL\n\n- (a) A complete **meta-programming language** (CWI/UseTheSource) for source analysis and\n  transformation: built-in grammars, parsing, traversal, rewriting. Repo:\n  <https://github.com/usethesource/rascal> (458 stars; site <https://www.rascal-mpl.org>).\n- (b) Immutable values; transformation via rewriting (`visit` returns new trees).\n- (c) Parse trees from Rascal's generalized parser are **fully concrete** (layout/comments are part\n  of the tree per grammar's layout definitions); ASTs via `implode` lose trivia.\n- (d) **Concrete-syntax pattern matching**: match parse trees with patterns written in the object\n  language inside quotes (`` (Expr)`<Expr a> + <Expr b>` ``), plus abstract patterns,\n  `visit`/`switch` strategies, and relational/comprehension queries over extracted facts.\n- (e) Yes: `visit` with insert, string templates, full GPL around it.\n- (f) Any language you define a grammar for (built-in grammar formalism, GLL parsing); library\n  grammars for Java (M3), C, etc.\n- (g) Define grammars + libraries in Rascal itself; Eclipse/VS Code IDE generation.\n- (h) BSD-2-Clause (verified from `LICENSE`; some older files Eclipse-licensed).\n- (i) Tests: `test/org/rascalmpl/` (JUnit drivers) but the bulk are **in-language test functions**\n  (`test bool ...`) under `src/org/rascalmpl/library/lang/**/tests/`, runnable by the interpreter;\n  also `test/org/rascalmpl/benchmark`.\n- (j) **Concrete-syntax quoting/antiquoting in patterns** for arbitrary user-defined grammars and\n  built-in relational analysis (M3 model) — the strongest academic analogue to meta-language's goal.\n\n## Spoofax / Stratego\n\n- (a) Language workbench (TU Delft/MetaBorg): SDF3 declarative syntax, **Stratego** rewriting\n  language, NaBL2/Statix name/type analysis. Repos: <https://github.com/metaborg/spoofax> (Apache-2.0\n  runtime), Spoofax 3 at <https://github.com/metaborg/spoofax-pie> (**unverified contents**), site\n  <https://spoofax.dev>.\n- (b) Terms (ATerms) are immutable; Stratego rewriting produces new terms.\n- (c) SGLR parse trees retain layout; typical pipelines work on ASTs with origin tracking\n  (\"origin terms\" link AST nodes back to source for layout-preserving unparse — **partially\n  unverified**, based on Spoofax docs).\n- (d)/(e) **Stratego**: rewrite rules + programmable **strategies** (`innermost`, `topdown`,\n  `try`, …) — full strategic term rewriting; concrete-syntax patterns supported in rules.\n- (f) Any language defined in SDF3.\n- (g) The whole point: define syntax, analysis, transforms, editor services declaratively.\n- (h) Apache-2.0.\n- (i) Tests: **SPT (Spoofax Testing language)** — a dedicated DSL where `.spt` files embed program\n  fragments and expectations (`parse succeeds`, `parse to <AST>`, resolution/type expectations);\n  framework at <https://github.com/metaborg/spt> (Apache-2.0, verified); JUnit-style tests in\n  `org.metaborg.core.test`.\n- (j) **A DSL for syntax tests** (SPT) with first-class expectations like `parse to` /\n  `resolve #1 to #2`, and **strategy combinators** for ordering rewrites — meta-language's\n  transforms have no traversal-strategy algebra yet.\n\n## TXL\n\n- (a) \"Source Transformation by Example\": grammar + by-example rewrite rules, a 30+-year-old\n  transformation language (Queen's University). Site: <https://www.txl.ca> — current release FreeTXL\n  10.8b (July 2022).\n- (b)/(c) Functional rewriting over parse trees; whole files are re-unparsed (formatting is governed\n  by grammar formatting cues, not preserved verbatim).\n- (d)/(e) TXL rules: patterns and replacements written in the **object language's own syntax**\n  (\"by example\"), with parameterized rules, guards (`where`), and grammar **overrides** to extend a\n  base grammar per-transformation.\n- (f) The TXL grammar collection covers many languages (C, Java, COBOL, …) —\n  <https://www.txl.ca/txl-resources.html>.\n- (g) Grammar redefinition/override mechanism.\n- (h) FreeTXL is free and freely distributable (binary; compiler/interpreter); **not** OSI\n  open-source in the usual sense — source availability **unverified**.\n- (i) Test suite not publicly browsable on GitHub (no canonical public repo found) — **nothing to\n  port directly**; example transforms ship with the distribution.\n- (j) **Grammar overrides**: locally extending a language's grammar just for one transformation\n  (e.g., adding markup constructs) — a powerful idea for meta-language's per-language grammars.\n\n## JetBrains MPS\n\n- (a) Projectional language workbench: programs are edited **directly as the AST** (no parsing);\n  editors project the model as text/tables/diagrams. Repo: <https://github.com/JetBrains/MPS>\n  (1.6k stars; docs <https://www.jetbrains.com/mps/>).\n- (b) Fully mutable model (the model *is* the persistence format, XML on disk).\n- (c) Lossless trivially — there is no concrete text to lose; but **cannot ingest arbitrary existing\n  source text** without separate importers.\n- (d) Model queries via generator/BaseLanguage query API and editor \"find usages\"; no textual query\n  language.\n- (e) Generators (model-to-model + model-to-text templates), refactorings, intentions.\n- (f) Any language built in MPS; composition of languages is a headline feature (embedding languages\n  without grammar conflicts).\n- (g) Define languages (structure/editor/typesystem/generator aspects); plugin ecosystem.\n- (h) Apache-2.0.\n- (i) Tests: in-repo MPS modules — `languages.test/languageDesign`, `testbench/`, plus MPS's own\n  test languages for editor/generator tests; tests are MPS models (XML), not portable text fixtures.\n- (j) **Grammar-conflict-free language composition/embedding** and projectional (multi-notation)\n  editing — meta-language's mixed-region links are the parsing-world cousin; MPS shows the\n  AST-first endgame.\n\n## Coccinelle\n\n- (a) Program matching/transformation for **C** (Inria), driven by **SmPL \"semantic patches\"** —\n  patch-like specs with metavariables; used heavily by the Linux kernel. Repo:\n  <https://github.com/coccinelle/coccinelle> (797 stars; OCaml).\n- (b)/(c) Internal C AST + control-flow graph; output is generated as a minimal patch, so untouched\n  code is preserved (patch-based, not reprint-based).\n- (d) **SmPL**: looks like a unified diff with `-`/`+` lines, metavariable declarations\n  (`@@ expression E; @@`), `...` for control-flow paths (matching is along CFG paths, not just\n  syntax), position variables, and rule dependencies.\n- (e) Yes — the semantic patch *is* the transform; `spatch` applies it across a codebase.\n- (f) C (plus experimental C++ — `cpptests/` dir in repo).\n- (g) Python/OCaml scripting hooks inside rules.\n- (h) GPL-2.0.\n- (i) Tests: `tests/` with ~1000 files in **triples**: `name.c` (input), `name.cocci` (semantic\n  patch), `name.res` (expected output) — verified (`a.c`/`a.cocci`/`a.res`, `62.*`, …). The single\n  most portable transform-test corpus format in this list.\n- (j) **Control-flow-aware `...` matching** (match along execution paths, not sibling lists) and\n  diff-shaped transform specs; also the input/patch/expected triple test format.\n\n---\n\n## Other notable projects (adjacent, verified 2026-06-10)\n\n- **Biome** (<https://github.com/biomejs/biome>, Apache-2.0, 25k stars): web toolchain whose CST is a\n  rust-analyzer-style **red/green lossless tree** (`biome_rowan`); error-resilient parsing where even\n  broken code round-trips. Baron's JSON FST].\n9. **Structural diff between two snapshots** with token-level change display — natural fit for\n   `NetworkSnapshot` forks [difftastic; Roslyn `GetChanges()`].\n10. **Quasiquote templates with placeholders** for building subtrees from code strings\n    [Babel `@babel/template`; Spoon patterns; Rascal concrete-syntax quoting].\n11. **Sandboxed plugin ABI (Wasm)** so third parties ship transforms safely [SWC].\n12. **Conservative reprint + parenthesization safety**: when a transform splices a subtree into a\n    new precedence context, auto-insert/drop parens; idempotent reprint (\"identity\") tests\n    [Recast `test/parens.ts`, `test/identity.ts`].\n13. **Codemod fixture convention**: `<transform>.input.x` / `<transform>.output.x` pairs with a\n    one-line `defineTest` [jscodeshift].\n14. **Typed trivia**: model whitespace/comments as typed fields per construct (not just generic\n    trivia links), plus **metadata providers** layering scope/type/position over the lossless tree\n    [LibCST].\n15. **Red/green persistent trees with structure sharing** for cheap snapshots and full-fidelity\n    `ToFullString()` even on error trees [Roslyn; rowan/Biome].\n16. **Type attribution in the lossless tree** and a parser-independent **TCK** other\n    implementations must pass [OpenRewrite `rewrite-java-tck`].\n17. **Traversal-strategy combinators** (`topdown`, `innermost`, `try`, fixpoint) as a transform\n    ordering algebra [Stratego/Spoofax; (The crate metadata points at `github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-json5`, which returns 404.) |\n\n### Non-tree-sitter lossless alternatives (for cross-checking or fallback)\n\n- TOML: [`toml_edit`](https://crates.io/crates/toml_edit) 0.25.12+spec-1.1.0 (2026-05-27) — the\n  format-preserving parser used by Cargo itself; a strong round-trip oracle for TOML fixtures.\n- JSON/JSONC: [`jsonc-parser`](https://crates.io/crates/jsonc-parser) 0.32.4 (2026-05-10) — CST\n  mode preserves comments/whitespace.\n- XML: [`quick-xml`](https://crates.io/crates/quick-xml) 0.40.1 (2026-05-15) — event-based,\n  round-trip-capable, not a CST.\n- CSV: [`csv`](https://crates.io/crates/csv) 1.4.0 (2025-10-17) — fast but lossy (no quote/spacing\n  preservation); only useful for semantic cross-checks.\n\n**Formats lacking a good tree-sitter crate today: CSV and JSON5** (both have grammars but stale\ncrates.io bindings pinned to tree-sitter 0.20). Everything else is adoptable as-is.\n\n---\n\n## Part B: links ecosystem storage targets\n\n### links-notation (LiNo text format)\n\nRepo: <https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation> — Unlicense, last push 2026-06-03,\nactive. It is a polyglot monorepo; per the README, parsers ship for **six languages**:\n\n| Language | Package |\n|---|---|\n| Rust | [`links-notation`](https://crates.io/crates/links-notation) **0.13.0** (published 2025-12-01) |\n| JavaScript | npm [`links-notation`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/links-notation) |\n| C# | NuGet [`Link.Foundation.Links.Notation`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Link.Foundation.Links.Notation) |\n| Python | PyPI [`links-notation`](https://pypi.org/project/links-notation/) |\n| Go | `github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/go` |\n| Java | Maven Central `io.github.link-foundation:links-notation` |\n\nRust entry point: `links_notation::parse_lino(\"papa (lovesMama: loves mama)\")`. The notation\ncovers doublets (2-tuples), triplets, arbitrary N-tuple sequences, named links (`id: a b`), and\nan indented (significant-whitespace) syntax equivalent to the inline parenthesized form. This is\nthe natural **text storage backend** for `meta-language`: a CST serialized as nested links.\n\n### doublets-rs (binary doublets store)\n\nRepo: <https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-rs> — Unlicense, last push 2026-05-29.\nCrate: [`doublets`](https://crates.io/crates/doublets) **0.4.0** (published 2026-05-29; 43 k\ndownloads). **Actively maintained** and — important change from its early history — now builds on\n**stable Rust** (`rust-version = \"1.85\"`, stable toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`). The README's\ninstall snippet still says `doublets = \"0.3.0\"` (stale doc; 0.4.0 is latest, and formal-ai also\npins 0.3.0). Workspace members: `doublets` (core), `doublets-decorators`, `doublets-ffi`.\n\nA link is `(index, source, target)` where every element is itself a link reference; generic over\nany unsigned integer (`u8`…`usize`). Storage backends: `mem::FileMapped` (memory-mapped file\npersistence — this is the **binary doublets** format issue #47 wants) and `mem::Global` (heap),\nwith `unit::Store` (combined region) and `split::Store` (separate data/index trees) layouts, via\n[`platform-mem`](https://crates.io/crates/platform-mem) 0.3.0 and\n[`platform-data`](https://crates.io/crates/platform-data) 2.0.0 (both republished 2026-04).\n\nThe Rust analog of C#'s `ILinks` is a **two-layer trait stack** (verified from\n`doublets/src/data/traits.rs`):\n\n```rust\npub trait Links<T: LinkReference>: Send + Sync {\n    fn constants(&self) -> &LinksConstants<T>;          // any/null constants\n    fn count_links(&self, query: &[T]) -> T;\n    fn create_links(&mut self, query: &[T], handler: WriteHandler<'_, T>) -> Result<Flow, Error<T>>;\n    fn each_links(&self, query: &[T], handler: ReadHandler<'_, T>) -> Flow;\n    fn update_links(&mut self, query: &[T], change: &[T], handler: WriteHandler<'_, T>) -> Result<Flow, Error<T>>;\n    fn delete_links(&mut self, query: &[T], handler: WriteHandler<'_, T>) -> Result<Flow, Error<T>>;\n}\n```\n\n- `Links<T>` — five raw operations over slice queries (`[index, source, target]` patterns with an\n  `any` wildcard constant) plus callback handlers returning `Flow::Continue/Break`. Read ops take\n  `&self`, write ops `&mut self`.\n- `Doublets<T>: Links<T>` — ergonomic defaults built entirely on the raw layer: `create()`,\n  `create_point()`, `create_link(s, t)`, `count()`, `count_by(query)`, `get_link(i)`,\n  `search(s, t)`, `each(..)`/`each_by(..)`, `update(..)`, `delete(..)`, `delete_all()`.\n- `DoubletsExt` — iterator (`iter()`, `each_iter(query)`) and optional rayon parallel extensions.\n\n**Verdict: viable as the binary backend.** Stable-Rust, active in 2026, slice-query model maps\n1:1 onto link-cli's match patterns, and `Send + Sync` is required of implementors.\n\n### doublets-web (WASM doublets)\n\nRepo: <https://github.com/linksplatform/doublets-web> — Unlicense, TypeScript + Rust/`wasm-pack`,\nlast push 2026-05-23. npm package [`doublets-web`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/doublets-web)\n**0.1.3** (last modified 2026-05-08): \"WebAssembly bindings for the LinksPlatform Doublets\nassociative storage library.\" JS API mirrors the Rust one in OOP form: `new LinksConstants()`,\n`new UnitedLinks(constants)`, `links.create()/update()/count(new Link(any, s, t))`. Live\nplayground: <https://linksplatform.github.io/doublets-web/>. Relevance: if `meta-language`\ntargets the `doublets` crate, a browser build path already exists; formal-ai names `DoubletsWeb`\nas one of its three `LinkStoreBackend` variants.\n\n### link-cli (match-and-substitute semantics)\n\nRepo: <https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli> — Unlicense, last push 2026-05-20. Dual\nimplementation: C# (NuGet `clink` + `Foundation.Data.Doublets.Cli`) and Rust\n([`link-cli`](https://crates.io/crates/link-cli) **0.2.7**, published 2026-05-20, docs at\n<https://docs.rs/link-cli>), plus a WASM browser workbench built on `doublets-web`.\n\nEvery CRUD operation is **one substitution operation** over LiNo patterns (explicitly framed as a\n[Markov algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Markov_algorithm), Turing-complete):\n`(match patterns) (substitution patterns)`.\n\n| Operation | Query | Reading |\n|---|---|---|\n| Create | `() ((1 1))` | nothing → link with source 1, target 1 (index assigned by store) |\n| Read | `((1: 1 1)) ((1: 1 1))` | identity substitution = no-op; with `--changes` it echoes matches |\n| Update | `((1: 1 1)) ((1: 1 2))` | same index on both sides → in-place change of target |\n| Delete | `((1 1)) ()` | match → nothing |\n\nVariables, named references, LiNo import/export, structure formatting, and (C#-only for now)\npersistent transformation triggers layer on top. This is the exact semantics issue #47's third\nAPI style should reproduce as a library API.\n\n### formal-ai (the primary consumer)\n\nRepo: <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai> — Unlicense, **very active** (pushed\n2026-06-10, the research date). \"100% symbolic, logical, and data driven formal language\nprocessor\" exposing OpenAI-shaped chat/HTTP interfaces without neural inference.\n\nHow it consumes a links engine (verified from `Cargo.toml` and `src/link_store.rs`):\n\n- Dependencies: `links-notation = \"0.13.0\"`, `lino-objects-codec = \"0.2.1\"`,\n  `lino-arguments = \"0.3\"`, `link-calculator = \"0.17.2\"` (crates.io latest 0.18.0), and\n  `doublets = \"0.3.0\"` + `platform-mem` **optional**, enabled by the default feature\n  `doublets-native`.\n- `src/link_store.rs` defines a swappable storage boundary: `trait LinkStore` with\n  `backend()`, `append_memory_event(..)`, `import_memory_links_notation(..)`,\n  `export_memory_links_notation()`; `enum LinkStoreBackend { LinoProjection, DoubletsRs,\n  DoubletsWeb }`. `.lino` text stays the deterministic, human-reviewable import/export\n  projection; doublets is the native physical store; browsers mirror via IndexedDB\n  (`src/web/memory.js`). Its `DoubletLink { index, from, to }` is a string-keyed doublet\n  projection.\n- Data it would feed through `meta-language`: `data/seed/*.lino` (30+ files — `concepts.lino`\n  46 KB, `hello-world-programs.lino` 46 KB, `facts.lino` 22 KB, `intent-routing.lino`,\n  per-domain `meanings-*.lino`, …), `data/benchmarks/industry-suite.lino` and\n  `coding-modification-suite.lino`, and `data/source-index.lino`. All use the indented untyped\n  format from `lino-objects-codec`, capped at 1500 lines per file by a check script.\n\nImplication for `meta-language`: matching formal-ai's existing stack means consuming\n`links-notation` 0.13 for text, `doublets` 0.3/0.4 behind a feature gate, and emitting\n`lino-objects-codec`-compatible indented output.\n\n### lino-objects-codec\n\nRepo: <https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec> — Unlicense, last push 2026-05-10.\nDual-published: npm [`lino-objects-codec`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lino-objects-codec)\n**0.4.0** (2026-05-10) and crates.io [`lino-objects-codec`](https://crates.io/crates/lino-objects-codec)\n**0.2.1** (2026-05-03; note Rust lags npm). Encodes/decodes structured objects to/from LiNo;\nformal-ai calls `lino_objects_codec::format::parse_indented`. For `meta-language`, this is the\nreference for *typed object* projections onto LiNo, distinct from raw link dumps.\n\n### Comparison: RDF triple stores (Oxigraph) vs doublets\n\n[Oxigraph](https://github.com/oxigraph/oxigraph) — crates.io [`oxigraph`](https://crates.io/crates/oxigraph)\n**0.5.8** (2026-04-28), MIT OR Apache-2.0 — is the mature Rust RDF/SPARQL store (214 k downloads,\nRocksDB-backed persistence, SPARQL 1.1).\n\nKey structural differences:\n\n| | RDF triples (Oxigraph) | Doublets (doublets-rs) |\n|---|---|---|\n| Unit | `(subject, predicate, object)` — fixed arity 3 | `index: (source, target)` — arity 2 plus identity |\n| Element types | heterogeneous atoms: IRIs, blank nodes, literals | **homogeneous**: every element is itself a link reference; values are links too |\n| Statement identity | a triple has no first-class id (reification/RDF-star needed to talk about a triple) | every link has an index and can be the source/target of other links — self-describing by construction |\n| N-ary data | predicates fixed at 3; n-ary needs reification patterns | any arity via nesting doublets (a triple ≈ 2 doublets, `(a, (b, c))`) |\n| Query | SPARQL (standard, rich, heavyweight) | `[index, source, target]` patterns with `any` wildcard; link-cli adds Markov-style substitution |\n\nOxigraph is the benchmark for maturity and standards interop, but its fixed-arity,\ntyped-atom model cannot represent a lossless CST as uniformly as doublets, where the \"everything\nis a link\" invariant matches `meta-language`'s self-describing links-network design. An RDF\nexport could later be a *projection*, not a core backend.\n\n---\n\n## Part C: API style patterns in Rust\n\nHow leading crates expose the same operations through multiple styles — and what `meta-language`\nshould copy.\n\n### 1. Core trait + ergonomic extension trait (the pattern doublets-rs itself uses)\n\n`doublets` layers `Links<T>` (5 raw slice-query methods) → `Doublets<T>` (default-implemented\nergonomic methods) → `DoubletsExt` (iterator adapters). The std-library analog is\n`Iterator`: one required method (`next`), ~75 default fluent adapters, and `Itertools` as an\nexternal extension trait. **Recommendation:** `meta-language` should define one raw trait per\nbackend capability and put *all three API styles* in default-implemented or extension layers, so\nevery style provably hits the same five primitive operations.\n\n### 2. syn / quote — direct typed AST vs macro DSL ([syn](https://crates.io/crates/syn) 2.0.117, [quote](https://crates.io/crates/quote) 1.0.45)\n\nThe same token stream is consumed via a fully typed AST (`syn::ItemFn`, direct field access,\nOOP-style) and produced via the `quote!` template DSL (declarative, pattern-shaped). syn also\nmodels read-only vs mutating vs consuming traversal as three parallel trait families:\n`visit::Visit<'ast>` (`&self`-style), `visit_mut::VisitMut` (`&mut`), `fold::Fold` (owned) — a\ndirect template for `meta-language`'s read-only vs mutable CST access.\n\n### 3. Database stack — three crates, three styles over the same SQL operations\n\n- [`sqlx`](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx) 0.9.0: raw SQL strings + compile-time-checked\n  `query!` macros — the \"match pattern as text\" style (closest analog to link-cli queries).\n- [`diesel`](https://crates.io/crates/diesel) 2.3.10: a typed, composable query-builder DSL\n  (`users.filter(name.eq(\"x\")).load(..)`) — fluent chaining with compile-time schema.\n- [`sea-orm`](https://crates.io/crates/sea-orm) 1.1.20 layered on\n  [`sea-query`](https://crates.io/crates/sea-query) 1.0.1: ActiveRecord-style OOP entity methods\n  (`Entity::find_by_id(..).one(db)`) generating into a runtime fluent builder, with a raw-SQL\n  escape hatch.\n\nThe lesson: all three coexist because they **lower into one executor layer**. For issue #47:\nfluent builder, direct methods, and LiNo match-substitute queries should all lower into the\n`Links<T>`-like primitive set.\n\n### 4. Builder style specifics\n\n[`derive_builder`](https://crates.io/crates/derive_builder) 0.20.2 (runtime-checked) and\n[`typed-builder`](https://crates.io/crates/typed-builder) 0.23.2 (compile-time typestate: missing\nrequired field = type error) show the two fluent-construction idioms. Typestate builders suit\n`meta-language`'s \"construct a link/CST node\" path where well-formedness can be static.\n\n### 5. Read-only vs mutable access modeling\n\n- **`&self` / `&mut self` method pairs** are the canonical split: `get`/`get_mut`,\n  `iter`/`iter_mut` (std collections), syn's `Visit`/`VisitMut`. Doublets follows it\n  (`each_links(&self, ..)` vs `update_links(&mut self, ..)`).\n- **Persistent (immutable) structures:** [`rpds`](https://crates.io/crates/rpds) 1.2.1\n  (actively maintained, published 2026-05-15) offers persistent vectors/maps with structural\n  sharing; [`im`](https://crates.io/crates/im) 15.1.0 is more popular historically but dormant\n  (last publish 2022-04-29). If `meta-language` wants cheap CST snapshots/undo, prefer `rpds`.\n- **Freeze pattern:** build with `&mut` (or a builder), then publish as `Arc<Frozen>` exposing\n  only `&self` methods — how `tree-sitter`'s own `Tree` works (parse mutates a parser; the\n  resulting tree is cheaply cloneable and read-only, with edits producing new trees).\n\n### Recommended structure for issue #47\n\n1. **Primitive trait** (`LinkStore`-like, mirroring `Links<T>`): `constants`, `count`, `create`,\n   `each`, `update`, `delete` over `[index, source, target]` patterns; `&self` for reads,\n   `&mut self` for writes. Implementations: in-memory native Rust types, LiNo text\n   (via `links-notation` 0.13 + `lino-objects-codec`), binary doublets (feature-gated\n   `doublets` 0.4 with `mem::FileMapped`).\n2. **Fluent layer** as a default-implemented extension trait (chaining, iterator adapters,\n   typestate builders for node construction).\n3. **Query layer** implementing link-cli's `(match) (substitution)` LiNo semantics as a library\n   API, parsed with `links-notation`, lowered onto the primitive trait — giving formal-ai (whose\n   `LinkStoreBackend` enum already names `LinoProjection | DoubletsRs | DoubletsWeb`) a drop-in\n   engine.\n"

Readonly/mutable engine configuration (R-1)\n\n**Problem.** `LinkNetwork` is always mutable; `NetworkSnapshot` provides\nimmutability only as an opt-in versioning pattern, not a user configuration.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Add an `AccessMode { ReadOnly, Mutable }` knob to `ParseConfiguration` and a\n  `LinkNetwork::freeze()` / `as_read_only()` boundary that yields a read-only\n  view type exposing only `&self` operations (parse, query, project,\n  reconstruct, verify).\n- Model the split the way the Rust ecosystem does (see\n  [`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part C §5): reads on a\n  shared reference, writes on `&mut self` or an explicit mutable fork, plus a\n  frozen wrapper type so misuse is a compile-time error where possible and a\n  configuration-checked runtime error at API boundaries.\n- Reuse `NetworkSnapshot`'s `Arc<LinkNetwork>` sharing for the frozen form so\n  the feature composes with existing snapshot versioning instead of adding a\n  second immutability mechanism.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/snapshots.rs`, `src/configuration.rs`; precedent: Roslyn's\nfully immutable red/green trees and rowan/cstree persistent trees\n([`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md)).\n\n## S-2: Data-exchange format grammars (R-3, R-4)\n\n**Problem.** No mainstream data-exchange format has a wired grammar; JSON,\nYAML, XML, TOML, CSV, INI, protobuf, GraphQL all fall back to plain-text\ntokens.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Adopt the verified-compatible tree-sitter grammar crates (all use the same\n  `tree-sitter-language ^0.1` binding model as the project's tree-sitter\n  0.25.8): `tree-sitter-json` 0.24.8, `tree-sitter-yaml` 0.7.2,\n  `tree-sitter-toml-ng` 0.7.0, `tree-sitter-xml` 0.7.0 (XML + DTD),\n  `tree-sitter-ini` 1.4.0, `tree-sitter-proto` 0.4.0, `tree-sitter-graphql`\n  0.1.0.\n- CSV and JSON5 lack modern-binding crates.io releases (both pin tree-sitter\n  ~0.20); vendor the upstream grammars or defer those two to a follow-up noted\n  in the roadmap (no silent gaps).\n- Add a `DATA_FORMAT_TARGETS` registry in `src/parity.rs` mirroring\n  `MARKUP_LANGUAGE_TARGETS`, with `LANGUAGE_FIXTURES` round-trip fixtures per\n  format and mixed-region detection (e.g. JSON in Markdown fences).\n\n**Reuse.** `src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs` grammar wiring pattern from PRs\n#26-#28 and #44-#46; crate table in\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part A.\n\n## S-3: Next programming-language grammar wave (R-2)\n\n**Problem.** 17 grammars are wired (TIOBE top-10 + Rust, Go, Ruby,\nTypeScript/TSX, HTML, CSS), but \"all popular programming languages\" extends\npast the current set: PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Perl are all in the\nTIOBE top-20 with maintained official tree-sitter grammars.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Wire `tree-sitter-php`, `tree-sitter-swift`, `tree-sitter-kotlin` (community,\n  verify binding generation), `tree-sitter-scala`, `tree-sitter-lua`, and\n  `tree-sitter-perl`, following the exact pattern of PR #44-#46.\n- Extend `PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_TARGETS` (or add a `TIOBE_11_20_TARGETS` tier)\n  plus per-language `LANGUAGE_FIXTURES` with UTF-8 and recovery cases.\n- Document the acquisition order and any grammar whose crates.io release pins\n  an old tree-sitter (vendor or defer explicitly).\n\n**Reuse.** Same adapter seam as S-2; TIOBE source already cited in\n`docs/parity-roadmap.md`.\n\n## S-4: Pluggable language-parser registry (R-17, R-18)\n\n**Problem.** `LinkNetwork::parse` hardwires `BuiltInLanguageParser`; users\ncannot register a new language, override a grammar, or replace parser\ndispatch, although the `LanguageParser` trait already exists.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Introduce a `ParserRegistry` (language key → `Arc<dyn LanguageParser>`) with\n  the built-in set pre-registered; `ParseConfiguration` gains a\n  `with_parser_registry(...)` override so every entry point honors it.\n- Follow TXL's \"grammar override\" idea and SWC's plugin lesson\n  ([`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md)): user\n  registrations shadow built-ins for the same key rather than forking the\n  pipeline.\n- Keep terminology translation at the boundary per `docs/parity-roadmap.md`:\n  registered parsers must produce links, not foreign ASTs.\n\n**Reuse.** `LanguageParser` trait in `src/language_parser.rs`,\n`QueryPredicateHost` extension precedent in `src/query.rs`.\n\n## S-5: Links-notation network serialization (R-7)\n\n**Problem.** LiNo parses in (`src/lino_parser.rs`) but arbitrary networks\ncannot be written back out as links-notation text; only\n`self_description_text` emits LiNo-style lines.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Implement `LinkNetwork::to_lino()` / `from_lino()` providing a total\n  serialization of any network (references, names, metadata links) with a\n  round-trip property test: `from_lino(to_lino(n))` is isomorphic to `n`.\n- Align the dialect with the `links-notation` Rust crate 0.13.0 (the reference\n  parser, also pinned by formal-ai) so emitted text is consumable by every\n  ecosystem parser; record any divergence as parity fixtures.\n- Reuse the doublets-style id discipline for unnamed links so binary and text\n  storage share one addressing scheme (prepares S-6).\n\n**Reuse.** `src/lino_parser.rs`, `links-notation` crate;\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part B.\n\n## S-6: Doublets binary storage backend (R-8, R-18) - blocked by 01, 05\n\n**Problem.** No binary links storage exists; `Cargo.toml` has no `doublets`\ndependency.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Extract a storage trait with `&self` reads / `&mut self` writes (S-1 defines\n  the access-mode semantics) covering create/read/update/delete/search over\n  links, with the in-memory `LinkNetwork` as the default implementation.\n- Add a feature-gated `doublets` backend using `doublets` 0.4.0 (published\n  2026-05-29, stable Rust 1.85, Unlicense, file-mapped persistence) and adopt\n  its own three-layer API precedent: raw `Links<T>` ops, ergonomic defaults,\n  iterator extensions.\n- Match formal-ai's `LinkStoreBackend` enum (LinoProjection, DoubletsRs,\n  DoubletsWeb) so meta-language can be dropped under it; doublets-web remains\n  out of process (WASM) and is documented as an exchange target via the same\n  binary layout rather than a linked dependency.\n- S-5's serializer provides the text↔binary bridge fixtures.\n\n**Reuse.** `doublets` crate; doublets-vs-RDF analysis in\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part B.\n\n## S-7: Rust types/traits ↔ links codec (R-9) - blocked by 05\n\n**Problem.** `LinkType::Object` and `insert_object` cover identity and\ncircular references, but arbitrary user structs/enums/traits cannot be encoded\nto links and decoded back.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Provide `ToLinks` / `FromLinks` traits with implementations for primitives,\n  `Vec`, `Option`, maps, and a `#[derive(Links)]` proc-macro (or a\n  serde-Serializer adapter writing into the network — decide in the issue;\n  serde adapter reuses the whole serde ecosystem at zero macro cost).\n- Keep parity with `lino-objects-codec` 0.2.1 (Rust) / 0.4.0 (npm): port its\n  shared-reference and circular-reference cases as fixtures; S-5's text form\n  makes the encoding inspectable.\n- Trait *types* (not just values): represent Rust type declarations as links\n  via the existing self-description roots (`type`, `Type`, `field`), so a\n  type's shape is itself queryable data.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/parity_fixtures.rs` lino-objects-codec fixtures,\n`src/self_description.rs`; serde precedent in\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part C.\n\n## S-8: Natural-language grammatical-correctness parsing (R-5)\n\n**Problem.** Natural-language support is identification + segmentation +\nscript annotations; nothing parses grammar, so grammatical correctness cannot\nbe checked. Issue #47 explicitly scopes semantics out and grammar in.\n\n**Plan** (staged; see\n[`competitors-natural-language.md`](./competitors-natural-language.md)\n\"Recommended approach signals\"):\n1. **Vocabulary first.** Adopt Universal Dependencies' UPOS/UFeats/deprel\n   inventory as link-type vocabulary for morphosyntax links; import CoNLL-U\n   with `rs-conllu` for fixtures and regression corpora (per-treebank licenses\n   recorded in provenance).\n2. **Word-level correctness.** Build morphological lexica from Wikidata\n   lexeme Forms (CC0) first and UniMorph TSV (CC BY-SA) second; an unknown or\n   wrongly inflected form is a recoverable `is_error` link, mirroring the\n   existing parse-recovery contract.\n3. **Sentence-level correctness.** Grammatical Framework is the only surveyed\n   system doing exactly this job (parse-or-reject, no semantics, RGL covers\n   the top-10 target languages, LGPL/BSD): compile RGL grammars to PGF and\n   read them from Rust (the young `gf-core` crate now; a native PMCFG reader\n   over the links network as the robust long-term path).\n4. **Explainable negatives.** Port LanguageTool-style pass/fail rule\n   sentences (LGPL; `nlprule` proves the Rust port) and DELPH-IN \"mal-rule\"\n   ideas so failures carry explanations, again as error links.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/natural_language.rs`, recovery flags in `src/link_flags.rs`;\n`NATURAL_LANGUAGE_TARGETS` gates extended with grammar fixtures per language.\n\n## S-9: Exact-match shared concept space (R-6)\n\n**Problem.** The 351-concept lexicon and `reference_for_atom` exact-`find_term`\nreuse exist, but concepts are not interned across languages with a stated\nexact-match discipline, and translation through concepts is demo-grade.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Copy Wikidata's two-layer design: language-bound lexeme links connected to\n  language-free concept links (all CC0, no licensing friction).\n- Institutionalize the issue's \"reuse only when matched exactly\" rule the way\n  WordNet CILI does: a concept is reused only on exact interlingual-id match,\n  otherwise a new concept link is minted; store ILI ids (CC BY) and Wikidata\n  Q-ids as alias links on concept links.\n- Generalize `seed_common_concept_ontology` into an import surface that can\n  load concept sets from LiNo files (S-5 format), keeping the 351-concept\n  seed as the default.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/concept_ontology.rs`, `src/lino_parser.rs`;\n[`competitors-natural-language.md`](./competitors-natural-language.md)\n\"Exact-match shared concept space\".\n\n## S-10: Configurable translation-rule registry (R-15, R-17) - blocked by 04, 09\n\n**Problem.** To-meta translation (parse) is total, but from-meta cross-language\noutput is gated on the hard-coded statehood proposition, and users cannot add\nor replace translation rules.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Replace the hard-coded gate with a `TranslationRuleSet`: ordered, named\n  rules mapping concept/structure patterns (LinkQuery-shaped left sides) to\n  per-language syntax templates (concept-to-language mappings generalized from\n  `insert_concept_mapping`).\n- Make every stage user-replaceable: rule sets are values (loadable from LiNo\n  via S-5, registrable like parsers via S-4's registry pattern), so end users\n  get the issue's \"full freedom of configuration\".\n- Quasiquote-style templates with placeholders (Babel `template`/GritQL\n  precedent in\n  [`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md)) keep\n  generated text aligned with grammar nodes rather than string concatenation.\n- Acceptance: the statehood demo becomes one rule set among others, and at\n  least one new translation pair runs entirely from user-supplied rules.\n\n## S-11: Single-language restriction profiles (R-16) - blocked by 10\n\n**Problem.** No way to restrict operations to \"only features of meta language\nthat JavaScript supports exactly\" for same-language (JS→JS) workflows.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Add `LanguageProfile` links: per-language capability sets naming which\n  concepts, link types, and translation rules a target language supports\n  (profiles are themselves links, hence queryable and user-editable).\n- `ParseConfiguration::with_profile(\"JavaScript\")` (or a transform-time\n  profile argument) makes any operation that would leave the profile fail with\n  a diagnostic link instead of producing untranslatable output.\n- Profiles compose with S-10 rule sets: a profile is effectively the domain of\n  the rule set, computed or declared.\n\n## S-12: Query/transform algebra enrichment (R-11 extension, richest feature set)\n\n**Problem.** `LinkQuery` covers type/term/language/named/S-expression/captures\nand `ReplacementRule`/`SubstitutionRule` cover replace-and-substitute, but the\ncompetitor survey shows a richer operator set users now expect.\n\n**Plan** (operators sourced from\n[`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md) \"Feature ideas\"):\n- Relational/composable rule algebra: `inside`, `has`, `precedes`, `follows`,\n  `all/any/not`, and named reusable sub-rules (ast-grep).\n- Ellipsis and typed metavariables: `...` gap matching and kind-constrained\n  captures (Semgrep, Coccinelle), plus grammar-less fallback matching for\n  unwired languages (Comby) — which meta-language can ground in its existing\n  plain-text token links.\n- Quasiquote replacement templates with placeholder safety and\n  parenthesization-conservative reprinting (Babel template, Recast).\n- Traversal-strategy combinators: `topdown`, `bottomup`, `innermost`,\n  `fixpoint` (Stratego/Rascal) over links.\n- A valid/invalid snapshot test harness for rules (ast-grep's YAML test idea)\n  to make rule suites self-verifying.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/query.rs`, `src/transform.rs`, `src/substitution.rs`.\n\n## S-13: Incremental re-parse and structural sharing (richest feature set)\n\n**Problem.** Every edit re-parses from scratch; competitors (tree-sitter\nincremental parsing, Roslyn/rowan red-green trees, difftastic structural diff)\ntreat incrementality and sharing as core.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Expose tree-sitter's native incremental parsing (`InputEdit` + old tree)\n  through the adapter: `LinkNetwork::apply_edit(range, new_text)` re-parses\n  only affected regions and reuses untouched links (ids stable outside the\n  edited span).\n- Extend `NetworkSnapshot` structural sharing so an edited fork shares\n  unchanged links with its parent (rowan/cstree precedent), and add a\n  structural diff between two snapshots (difftastic precedent) returning\n  changed-link sets — which also gives transforms cheap dry-run previews.\n\n**Reuse.** tree-sitter 0.25 incremental API already in the dependency tree;\n`src/snapshots.rs`.\n\n## S-14: API-style parity contract (R-12, R-13, R-14) - blocked by 06, 10\n\n**Problem.** Operations are unevenly reachable: queries have builder +\nS-expression forms, substitutions only direct methods; nothing guarantees \"all\noperations in all styles\".\n\n**Plan.**\n- Declare the operation inventory as data: an `API_OPERATIONS` registry\n  (parse, query, transform, substitute, serialize, snapshot, translate,\n  verify, ...) × style (direct method, fluent chain, link-cli substitution,\n  S-expression/LiNo text) — the same registry-plus-gate pattern the crate\n  already uses for languages and parity targets.\n- Implement the missing styles: a fluent pipeline (`network.find(q).replace(r)\n  .reconstruct()` — jscodeshift precedent) as a default-implemented extension\n  trait over the storage trait from S-6 (sqlx/diesel/sea-orm layering: many\n  styles, one executor), and link-cli-style text operations for each\n  operation where applicable (link-cli 0.2.7 semantics: create `() ((1 1))`,\n  delete `((1 1)) ()`, update same-index, read identity).\n- Gate it: a unit test iterates `API_OPERATIONS` and asserts each operation\n  has an executable fixture per style, so the matrix can never silently\n  regress (this is the R-14 contract).\n\n## S-15: Competitor corpora wave 2 + coverage gate (R-19, R-20) - blocked by 02, 08, 12, 14\n\n**Problem.** 48 ported fixtures are a small fraction of upstream suites; the\nllvm-cov job enforces no threshold; the roadmap still defers SQL dialects and\nDelphi-specific coverage.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Port the five highest-value suites identified in\n  [`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md): Coccinelle\n  `tests/` transform triples, tree-sitter `test/corpus` + `error_corpus`,\n  Semgrep `tests/patterns/<lang>/`, srcML `test/parser/testsuite` round-trip\n  cases, LibCST adversarial whitespace fixtures (runner-up: babel-parser\n  fixtures) — each as provenanced `PARITY_FIXTURES`, sampled per construct\n  rather than wholesale where suites are huge, with sampling documented.\n- Add new `PARITY_TARGETS` for the surveyed competitors not yet tracked\n  (ast-grep, Semgrep, Comby, GritQL, srcML, difftastic, Babel, SWC,\n  OpenRewrite, Spoon, JavaParser, Rascal, Stratego/Spoofax, TXL, MPS,\n  Coccinelle; plus GF, UD, LanguageTool from the natural-language survey, and\n  doublets-rs/links-notation storage gates) so the \"all competitors in all\n  scopes\" comparison is executable, not prose.\n- Turn the existing `cargo llvm-cov` job into a ratcheted gate: record current\n  line coverage, fail CI below the recorded floor, raise the floor with each\n  wave toward the issue's 100% goal; audit `docs/parity-roadmap.md` so every\n  deferral is either implemented or tracked by an open issue (R-19).\n\n## Phasing\n\n- **Phase 1 (parallel, no dependencies):** 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 08, 09, 12, 13.\n- **Phase 2:** 06 (after 01, 05), 07 (after 05), 10 (after 04, 09).\n- **Phase 3:** 11 (after 10), 14 (after 06, 10).\n- **Phase 4:** 15 (after 02, 08, 12, 14) — the closing audit/coverage gate.\n\nIssue #47 instructs that all sub-issue work lands on the issue-47 branch and\nmerges through one pull request ([PR #48](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/48)).\n"

Readonly/mutable engine configuration (R-1)\n\n**Problem.** `LinkNetwork` is always mutable; `NetworkSnapshot` provides\nimmutability only as an opt-in versioning pattern, not a user configuration.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Add an `AccessMode { ReadOnly, Mutable }` knob to `ParseConfiguration` and a\n  `LinkNetwork::freeze()` / `as_read_only()` boundary that yields a read-only\n  view type exposing only `&self` operations (parse, query, project,\n  reconstruct, verify).\n- Model the split the way the Rust ecosystem does (see\n  [`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part C §5): reads on a\n  shared reference, writes on `&mut self` or an explicit mutable fork, plus a\n  frozen wrapper type so misuse is a compile-time error where possible and a\n  configuration-checked runtime error at API boundaries.\n- Reuse `NetworkSnapshot`'s `Arc<LinkNetwork>` sharing for the frozen form so\n  the feature composes with existing snapshot versioning instead of adding a\n  second immutability mechanism.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/snapshots.rs`, `src/configuration.rs`; precedent: Roslyn's\nfully immutable red/green trees and rowan/cstree persistent trees\n([`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md)).\n\n## S-2: Data-exchange format grammars (R-3, R-4)\n\n**Problem.** No mainstream data-exchange format has a wired grammar; JSON,\nYAML, XML, TOML, CSV, INI, protobuf, GraphQL all fall back to plain-text\ntokens.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Adopt the verified-compatible tree-sitter grammar crates (all use the same\n  `tree-sitter-language ^0.1` binding model as the project's tree-sitter\n  0.25.8): `tree-sitter-json` 0.24.8, `tree-sitter-yaml` 0.7.2,\n  `tree-sitter-toml-ng` 0.7.0, `tree-sitter-xml` 0.7.0 (XML + DTD),\n  `tree-sitter-ini` 1.4.0, `tree-sitter-proto` 0.4.0, `tree-sitter-graphql`\n  0.1.0.\n- CSV and JSON5 lack modern-binding crates.io releases (both pin tree-sitter\n  ~0.20); vendor the upstream grammars or defer those two to a follow-up noted\n  in the roadmap (no silent gaps).\n- Add a `DATA_FORMAT_TARGETS` registry in `src/parity.rs` mirroring\n  `MARKUP_LANGUAGE_TARGETS`, with `LANGUAGE_FIXTURES` round-trip fixtures per\n  format and mixed-region detection (e.g. JSON in Markdown fences).\n\n**Reuse.** `src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs` grammar wiring pattern from PRs\n#26-#28 and #44-#46; crate table in\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part A.\n\n## S-3: Next programming-language grammar wave (R-2)\n\n**Problem.** 17 grammars are wired (TIOBE top-10 + Rust, Go, Ruby,\nTypeScript/TSX, HTML, CSS), but \"all popular programming languages\" extends\npast the current set: PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Perl are all in the\nTIOBE top-20 with maintained official tree-sitter grammars.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Wire `tree-sitter-php`, `tree-sitter-swift`, `tree-sitter-kotlin` (community,\n  verify binding generation), `tree-sitter-scala`, `tree-sitter-lua`, and\n  `tree-sitter-perl`, following the exact pattern of PR #44-#46.\n- Extend `PROGRAMMING_LANGUAGE_TARGETS` (or add a `TIOBE_11_20_TARGETS` tier)\n  plus per-language `LANGUAGE_FIXTURES` with UTF-8 and recovery cases.\n- Document the acquisition order and any grammar whose crates.io release pins\n  an old tree-sitter (vendor or defer explicitly).\n\n**Reuse.** Same adapter seam as S-2; TIOBE source already cited in\n`docs/parity-roadmap.md`.\n\n## S-4: Pluggable language-parser registry (R-17, R-18)\n\n**Problem.** `LinkNetwork::parse` hardwires `BuiltInLanguageParser`; users\ncannot register a new language, override a grammar, or replace parser\ndispatch, although the `LanguageParser` trait already exists.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Introduce a `ParserRegistry` (language key → `Arc<dyn LanguageParser>`) with\n  the built-in set pre-registered; `ParseConfiguration` gains a\n  `with_parser_registry(...)` override so every entry point honors it.\n- Follow TXL's \"grammar override\" idea and SWC's plugin lesson\n  ([`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md)): user\n  registrations shadow built-ins for the same key rather than forking the\n  pipeline.\n- Keep terminology translation at the boundary per `docs/parity-roadmap.md`:\n  registered parsers must produce links, not foreign ASTs.\n\n**Reuse.** `LanguageParser` trait in `src/language_parser.rs`,\n`QueryPredicateHost` extension precedent in `src/query.rs`.\n\n## S-5: Links-notation network serialization (R-7)\n\n**Problem.** LiNo parses in (`src/lino_parser.rs`) but arbitrary networks\ncannot be written back out as links-notation text; only\n`self_description_text` emits LiNo-style lines.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Implement `LinkNetwork::to_lino()` / `from_lino()` providing a total\n  serialization of any network (references, names, metadata links) with a\n  round-trip property test: `from_lino(to_lino(n))` is isomorphic to `n`.\n- Align the dialect with the `links-notation` Rust crate 0.13.0 (the reference\n  parser, also pinned by formal-ai) so emitted text is consumable by every\n  ecosystem parser; record any divergence as parity fixtures.\n- Reuse the doublets-style id discipline for unnamed links so binary and text\n  storage share one addressing scheme (prepares S-6).\n\n**Reuse.** `src/lino_parser.rs`, `links-notation` crate;\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part B.\n\n## S-6: Doublets binary storage backend (R-8, R-18) - blocked by 01, 05\n\n**Problem.** No binary links storage exists; `Cargo.toml` has no `doublets`\ndependency.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Extract a storage trait with `&self` reads / `&mut self` writes (S-1 defines\n  the access-mode semantics) covering create/read/update/delete/search over\n  links, with the in-memory `LinkNetwork` as the default implementation.\n- Add a feature-gated `doublets` backend using `doublets` 0.4.0 (published\n  2026-05-29, stable Rust 1.85, Unlicense, file-mapped persistence) and adopt\n  its own three-layer API precedent: raw `Links<T>` ops, ergonomic defaults,\n  iterator extensions.\n- Match formal-ai's `LinkStoreBackend` enum (LinoProjection, DoubletsRs,\n  DoubletsWeb) so meta-language can be dropped under it; doublets-web remains\n  out of process (WASM) and is documented as an exchange target via the same\n  binary layout rather than a linked dependency.\n- S-5's serializer provides the text↔binary bridge fixtures.\n\n**Reuse.** `doublets` crate; doublets-vs-RDF analysis in\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part B.\n\n## S-7: Rust types/traits ↔ links codec (R-9) - blocked by 05\n\n**Problem.** `LinkType::Object` and `insert_object` cover identity and\ncircular references, but arbitrary user structs/enums/traits cannot be encoded\nto links and decoded back.\n\n**Plan.**\n- Provide `ToLinks` / `FromLinks` traits with implementations for primitives,\n  `Vec`, `Option`, maps, and a `#[derive(Links)]` proc-macro (or a\n  serde-Serializer adapter writing into the network — decide in the issue;\n  serde adapter reuses the whole serde ecosystem at zero macro cost).\n- Keep parity with `lino-objects-codec` 0.2.1 (Rust) / 0.4.0 (npm): port its\n  shared-reference and circular-reference cases as fixtures; S-5's text form\n  makes the encoding inspectable.\n- Trait *types* (not just values): represent Rust type declarations as links\n  via the existing self-description roots (`type`, `Type`, `field`), so a\n  type's shape is itself queryable data.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/parity_fixtures.rs` lino-objects-codec fixtures,\n`src/self_description.rs`; serde precedent in\n[`formats-storage-apis.md`](./formats-storage-apis.md) Part C.\n\n## S-8: Natural-language grammatical-correctness parsing (R-5)\n\n**Problem.** Natural-language support is identification + segmentation +\nscript annotations; nothing parses grammar, so grammatical correctness cannot\nbe checked. Issue #47 explicitly scopes semantics out and grammar in.\n\n**Plan** (staged; see\n[`competitors-natural-language.md`](./competitors-natural-language.md)\n\"Recommended approach signals\"):\n1. **Vocabulary first.** Adopt Universal Dependencies' UPOS/UFeats/deprel\n   inventory as link-type vocabulary for morphosyntax links; import CoNLL-U\n   with `rs-conllu` for fixtures and regression corpora (per-treebank licenses\n   recorded in provenance).\n2. **Word-level correctness.** Build morphological lexica from Wikidata\n   lexeme Forms (CC0) first and UniMorph TSV (CC BY-SA) second; an unknown or\n   wrongly inflected form is a recoverable `is_error` link, mirroring the\n   existing parse-recovery contract.\n3. **Sentence-level correctness.** Grammatical Framework is the only surveyed\n   system doing exactly this job (parse-or-reject, no semantics, RGL covers\n   the top-10 target languages, LGPL/BSD): compile RGL grammars to PGF and\n   read them from Rust (the young `gf-core` crate now; a native PMCFG reader\n   over the links network as the robust long-term path).\n4. **Explainable negatives.** Port LanguageTool-style pass/fail rule\n   sentences (LGPL; `nlprule` proves the Rust port) and DELPH-IN \"mal-rule\"\n   ideas so failures carry explanations, again as error links.\n\n**Reuse.** `src/natural_language.rs`, recovery flags in `src/link_flags.rs`;\n`NATURAL_LANGUAGE_TARGETS` gates extended with grammar fixtures per language.\n\n## S-9: Exact-match shared concept space (R-6)\n\n**Problem.** The 351-concept lexicon and \"reuse only when matched exactly\" rule the way\n  WordNet CILI does: a concept is reused only on exact interlingual-id match,\n  otherwise a new concept link is minted; store ILI ids (CC BY) and space\".\n\n## S-10: Configurable translation-rule registry (R-15, R-17) - blocked by 04, 09\n\n**Problem.** To-meta translation (parse) is total, but from-meta cross-language\noutput is gated on the S-11: Single-language restriction profiles (R-16) - blocked by 10\n\n**Problem.** No way to restrict operations to \"only features of meta language\nthat JavaScript supports exactly\" for reusable sub-rules (ast-grep).\n- Ellipsis and typed metavariables: `...` gap matching and kind-constrained\n  captures (Semgrep, Coccinelle), plus grammar-less fallback matching for\n  unwired re-parses\n  only affected regions and reuses untouched links (ids stable outside the\n  edited span).\n- Extend `NetworkSnapshot` structural sharing so an edited fork shares\n  unchanged links with Current support is\nidentification, segmentation, normalization, and script annotations\n(`src/natural_language.rs`) - nothing parses grammar, so correctness cannot be\nchecked. See [`requirements.md`](../requirements.md) **R-5** and\n[`solution-plans.md`](../solution-plans.md) **S-8**.\n\nResearch ([`competitors-natural-language.md`](../competitors-natural-language.md)):\nGrammatical Framework + Resource Grammar Library is the only surveyed system\ndoing exactly this job (parse-or-reject, no semantics, covers the ten target\nlanguages, LGPL/BSD); UD supplies the morphosyntax vocabulary and corpora;\nWikidata lexemes (CC0) and UniMorph (CC BY-SA) supply word forms; LanguageTool\n(LGPL, proven portable to Rust by nlprule) supplies explainable negative\nchecks.\n\n## Scope (staged)\n\n1. Adopt UD's UPOS/UFeats/deprel inventory as link-type vocabulary for\n   morphosyntax links; import CoNLL-U fixtures (e.g. via `rs-conllu`) with\n   per-treebank license provenance.\n2. Word-level correctness: morphological lexica seeded from Wikidata lexeme\n   Forms (CC0; UniMorph optional second source); unknown/ill-formed tokens\n   become recoverable `is_error` links, reusing the parse-recovery contract.\n3. The largest gaps: no data-exchange format\n  grammars, no binary doublets storage, no grammatical-correctness parsing\n  for natural languages, no engine-level readonly configuration, no general\n  network→LiNo serializer, cross-language translation gated on a hard-coded\n  demo, and no API-style parity contract. See\n  [`requirements.md`](./requirements.md).\n- **Code tooling:** 22 competitor projects surveyed. Top capabilities to\n  match: incremental re-parse and red/green structural sharing (tree-sitter,\n  Roslyn, rowan), composable rule algebra and snapshot rule tests (ast-grep),\n  ellipsis/typed metavariables (Semgrep, Coccinelle), quasiquote templates\n  and conservative reprinting (Babel, Recast), traversal strategies\n  (Stratego, Rascal), grammar-less fallback (Comby), structural diff\n  (difftastic). See\n  [`competitors-code-tooling.md`](./competitors-code-tooling.md).\n- **Natural language:** Grammatical Framework + Resource Grammar Library is\n  the only surveyed system doing exactly the issue's job - parse-or-reject\n  grammaticality with no semantics, covering the ten target languages\n  (LGPL/BSD). UD supplies the morphosyntax vocabulary and corpora; Wikidata\n  lexemes (CC0) and WordNet CILI ids (CC BY) supply the exact-match concept\n  discipline; LanguageTool/nlprule supply explainable negative checks;\n  BabelNet is rejected on licensing. See\n  [`competitors-natural-language.md`](./competitors-natural-language.md).\n- **Formats and storage:** seven tree-sitter format grammars are\n  drop-in-compatible with the project's tree-sitter 0.25.8 (JSON, YAML,\n  TOML, XML, INI, protobuf, GraphQL); CSV and JSON5 need vendoring.\n  `doublets` 0.4.0 is a viable binary backend (stable Rust, Unlicense,\n  file-mapped persistence), and formal-ai - the heaviest planned user -\n  already defines a `LinkStoreBackend { LinoProjection, DoubletsRs,\n  DoubletsWeb }` stack to match.
